title: test(cli): pin the app-generator's workspace/standalone branches explicitly
body:
Fixes #7807

## What this adds

Two cases in `app-generator.test.ts`'s `generation onto disk` block. **The existing two
are untouched** — the only removed line in the entire diff is the `vitest` import line,
which gains `vi`; everything else is pure insertion.

```ts
function writingFrom(cwd: string, write: () => void): void {
  const stub = vi.spyOn(process, 'cwd').mockReturnValue(cwd);
  try { write(); } finally { stub.mockRestore(); }
}

it('writes the IN-WORKSPACE map when the generator runs at a workspace root', () => {
  withTempDir((dir) => {
    writingFrom(REPO_ROOT, () => createTempApp(dir, SCHEMA));
    expect(filesOnDisk(dir)).toEqual(buildAppFiles(SCHEMA, IN_WORKSPACE));
  });
});

it('writes the STANDALONE map when the generator runs outside a workspace', () => {
  withTempDir((dir) => {
    writingFrom(dir, () => createTempApp(dir, SCHEMA));
    expect(filesOnDisk(dir)).toEqual(buildAppFiles(SCHEMA, { cwd: dir, isMonorepo: false }));
  });
});
```

Both roots are file-derived: `REPO_ROOT` is the file's existing
`resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../../../..')` — the spelling PR #7796
landed and #7806 reused, not a third one — and the standalone case names the same
`mkdtemp` directory on both sides. Neither reads the ambient cwd, so each pins the same
branch under every invocation.

### Why the cwd is stubbed rather than changed

`createTempApp` derives its own context inside `currentContext()` from `process.cwd()`
and takes no context argument, so the branch can only be selected through `process.cwd()`.
`process.chdir()` is not the available lever here: the `unit` project runs `pool: 'threads'`
and Node throws `ERR_WORKER_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION: process.chdir() is not supported in
workers` (measured in this container with a `worker_threads` probe). The stub therefore
covers exactly the one synchronous writer call and is restored in a `finally`.

### Why a second case, pinning STANDALONE

One explicit IN-WORKSPACE case alone would not equalise coverage: from the repo root the
ambient pair also pins IN-WORKSPACE, leaving STANDALONE still unreached in CI. With both
explicit cases the covered set is `{IN-WORKSPACE, STANDALONE}` under either invocation,
which is the issue's acceptance criterion. They are two separate, each-explicit cases —
which branch each pins never depends on cwd.

## Both-cwd readings, before and after

The file, run under each invocation (`git rev-parse --short HEAD` = `afa1722c9`):

| invocation | cwd | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/cli/src/__tests__/app-generator.test.ts` | repo root | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 41 passed (41)`, exit 0 | `1 passed (1)` / `43 passed (43)`, exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run --root ../.. packages/cli/src/__tests__/app-generator.test.ts` | `packages/cli` | `1 passed (1)` / `41 passed (41)`, exit 0 | `1 passed (1)` / `43 passed (43)`, exit 0 |

The second row is the package-dir invocation narrowed to this one file. The criterion's
unnarrowed form was run too — `pnpm --filter @object-ui/cli test`, whole package, cwd
`packages/cli`: **before** `Test Files 16 passed (16)` / `Tests 246 passed (246)`, exit 0;
**after** `Test Files 16 passed (16)` / `Tests 248 passed (248)`, exit 0. (An extra path
argument cannot narrow that form — Vitest unions positional filters with the script's own
`packages/cli/`, so all 16 files still run; hence the explicit `--root ../..` spelling
above, which reproduces the same cwd with a narrower filter.)

41 to 43 in both columns, +2 exactly, **no case going from passing to failing**. Verbose
listing of the block at `afa1722c9`, repo root:

```
✓ generation onto disk > writes exactly the plain app file map, byte for byte
✓ generation onto disk > writes exactly the routed app file map, byte for byte
✓ generation onto disk > writes the IN-WORKSPACE map when the generator runs at a workspace root
✓ generation onto disk > writes the STANDALONE map when the generator runs outside a workspace
✓ generation onto disk > writes a manifest whose @object-ui ranges name this CLI version
```

## Lit control

Mutation: the new IN-WORKSPACE case's root derivation put back to an ambient-cwd form,
`writingFrom(REPO_ROOT, …)` to `writingFrom(process.cwd(), …)`, one occurrence, run under
`trap '… git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH' EXIT INT TERM`.

Mutation confirmed on disk before either leg ran — anchor counts flipped
(`OLD=1 NEW=0` to `OLD=0 NEW=1`) and the blob hash moved:

```
HEAD_BLOB=f50502442602fdc45a8cf07df185283cc4060158
PRE_HASH =f50502442602fdc45a8cf07df185283cc4060158   (equal — tree was at HEAD)
MUT_HASH =f9c5acd8baa1096eed34f439a14b6656296b23ea   (differs — mutation landed)
```

| leg | cwd | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A | `packages/cli` | **RED, names itself** — `FAIL … generation onto disk > writes the IN-WORKSPACE map when the generator runs at a workspace root`, `AssertionError: expected { …(8) } to deeply equal { …(8) }`, `Tests 1 failed \| 42 passed (43)`, exit 1 |
| B | repo root | green, `43 passed (43)`, exit 0 |

Leg B is the finding restated: under the ambient form the repo-root run — the only form CI
runs — stays green while the branch it pins has silently changed. That is precisely why
the case must name its root.

Restoration proved by **state**, not by whether the trap fired:

```
POST_HASH=f50502442602fdc45a8cf07df185283cc4060158   (equal to HEAD_BLOB)
git diff HEAD --stat  -> 0 bytes
git status --porcelain -> empty
```

No rebuild leg applies: the test imports the subject as `../utils/app-generator.js`, a
relative source specifier Vite resolves to the `.ts` source, so no `dist/` artifact sits
between the mutation and the run.

## Type-check, through turbo

```
pnpm exec turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/cli --concurrency=2
Tasks:    10 successful, 10 total     exit 0
```

A bare `tsc --noEmit` is not this repo's gate — the turbo task `dependsOn ^build`, so the
run above is the one that means something.

## Changeset gate

Ran `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`. Verdict before, verbatim:

```
❌  1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change adds no changeset:
```

Owed, so `.changeset/cli-app-generator-explicit-branch-cases.md` was added with an **empty
frontmatter**. Verdict after, verbatim:

```
✅  1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s): .changeset/cli-app-generator-explicit-branch-cases.md.
    Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter — declared as releasing nothing, which
    is the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate.
```

`node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` also green: `✅  No changeset declares a
major bump.`

## Scope

Two files, taken from the recorded base `a617bb8d3` (not from a two-dot
`origin/main..HEAD` diff): `packages/cli/src/__tests__/app-generator.test.ts` and the
changeset. No non-test file under any `packages/*/src` was touched — `createTempApp` and
`contextOfCurrentProcess` are unchanged — and `packages/cli/package.json`'s `test` script
is untouched, so objectui#7800's devx decision stays open and undisturbed. ESLint on the
changed file: 1 file linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings (repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run).

Refs: objectui#7799 (the card this was split out of) · PR #7806 (the probe readings) ·
objectui#7800 (`test` script cwd devx decision, still open) · PR #7796 (the
`import.meta.url` walk-up spelling reused here).
